newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lesotho premier seeks court order -- S.Africa radio.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho premier seeks court order -- S.Africa radio.

text.p: Lesotho's 78-year-old premier, Ntsu Mokhehle, hit back against his Basotholand Congress Party on Wednesday with a court application challenging attempts to oust him as party leader, South African state radio reported.

In his application for an injunction to the High Court, Mokhehle argued the BCP resolution to dismiss him was detrimental to peace and stability in the kingdom due to his dual role as party leader and premier.

Mokhehle was sacked by his own party two weeks ago amid accusations that the country was drifting into lawlessness. The BCP resolved at its general conference "to relieve Dr Ntsu Mokhehle of his leadership of the BCP with immediate effect".
Diplomats said BCP deputy leader Matlejane Qhobela would be entitled to become prime minister under the party constitution, ahead of current Deputy Prime Minister Pakalitha Mosisili.

Qhobela, who is not in Mokhehle's cabinet, is believed to lead a pressure group in the ruling party, which has been lobbying for a leadership change ahead of a general election scheduled for next year.
The monarch, King Letsie III, was expected to call a meeting of the southern African country's Council of State to deal with the leadership crisis, but no date for the meeting has been set.

Mokhehle, despite the internal party wrangling and his poor health, has weathered a series of crises since March 1993 when he won the first democratic polls in two decades, as late as last month when a 11-day police munity was crushed by the army.
Diplomats told Reuters that Mokhehle retained strong support among voters and party members, and was not necessarily a spent force.
